source.title: Capturing Polysemanticity with PRISM: A Multi-Concept Feature Description Framework
source.authors: Laura Kopf; Nils Feldhus; Kirill Bykov; P. Bommer; Anna Hedstrom; M. Höhne; Oliver Eberle

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether feature descriptions predict activations on newly generated text using activation-distribution scores, a different measurement from the audit claim.
record.gate_note: The paper measures description quality and polysemanticity, not the share of neuron poles with one, two, or unknown jobs. Its main activation-based evaluation uses 1,000 random Cosmopedia texts as controls and 10 LLM-generated texts for each description. Table 1 reports means across selected features from early, middle, and late layers; Table 4 varies the description generator; Table 5 varies the evaluation text generator; Table 6 reports randomized-description controls.
record.test_reason: The study scores LLM-written descriptions of GPT-2 XL and Llama 3.1 8B MLP neurons. The descriptions come from top-activating examples, and the test is whether they make the neuron fire on new description-generated text versus random Cosmopedia controls (AUROC, % positive MAD). This is a different method aimed at V6's question: whether explanations drawn from activating examples predict where a neuron fires. It is not simulation scoring and sets no good-score cutoff, so V7 is not tested. SAE-feature results are a different unit (not neurons).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that multi-concept PRISM descriptions beat single-description methods on AUROC/MAD, and that many features encode diverse concepts. Neuron features are more reliably interpreted than SAE features, quality varies by architecture and layer (peaking mid-layer), and PRISM polysemanticity scores align with human judgments.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than counting single-job neuron poles, the paper clusters highly activating text examples into five groups, generates one description per cluster, and scores descriptions by comparing activations on generated concept text with random controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Description scores vary with model and feature type, PRISM mean versus max aggregation, evaluation text generator, and activation interval. The paper also reports variation across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Polysemanticity scores (cosine similarity among 5 cluster descriptions) vary by model, show no layer trend, and agree with human ratings on 8 features. Llama neuron descriptions sit near the random-description baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clustering a neuron's top activations yields semantically diverse descriptions for many LLM neurons, a measure of multi-concept structure rather than a share of one-job neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features (GPT-2 Small, Gemma Scope) score lower than MLP neurons (PRISM mean AUROC 0.43-0.51); the authors say neurons yield more reliable interpretations than SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-example descriptions predict neuron firing better than SAE-feature firing.

record.problems: The paper evaluates selected features, with 60 randomly selected features per model except GPT-2 Small SAE, which has 59. The scores are aggregate means rather than per-feature distributions or the fraction passing a declared threshold. PRISM uses five fixed clusters, which the authors note cannot guarantee that all or the most salient concepts are captured. Evaluation uses LLM-generated concept samples and may vary with the evaluation generator.
record.rows_left_out: None of the directly relevant Table 1, Table 4, Table 5, or Table 6 results were left out.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or shares of one-job/two-job/unknown neuron poles.
No share estimates across dense/MoE models or scale.
No vision models or the cat-and-car neuron.
No test of architecture or regularization effects or of tool improvement on interpretable share.
Tested only with LLM-generated concept text and random controls, not natural held-out activations. Only 60 random neurons per model, in 3 layers.
No simulation-based scoring and no good-score threshold or fraction of neurons passing one. Explainer strength is varied only via description generators, without a threshold.

missing.what: Baseline description methods on neurons: GPT-Explain (the Bills et al. explanations) on GPT-2 XL, AUROC 0.64 with 65% positive MAD. MaxAct gives 0.53/11.86% on GPT-2 XL and 0.54/50% on Llama. Transluce gives 0.59/63.33% and Output-Centric 0.55/58.33% on Llama.
GPT-Explain scores under alternative evaluation generators: AUROC 0.54-0.60.
Single description per neuron (k=1) on GPT-2 XL: AUROC 0.75 with 80% positive MAD; k=3 and k=10 variants also reported.
Description quality drops for lower percentile intervals (0.0-0.25 max AUROC 0.69).
Per-neuron AUROC distributions, needed for the share of neurons with poor scores.
Output-centric faithfulness for GPT-2 XL descriptions is low in absolute terms (below about 0.12).

record.verdict_notes: The test is a generated-text contrastive score (CoSy), not natural held-out activations or simulation, so V7 is untested. PRISM max is optimistic because it picks the best of 5 descriptions on the evaluation score. Table 4/5/6 rows partly duplicate Table 1 defaults. Gemma Scope rows mislabel the subject (it is an SAE suite on Gemma 2). The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the Qwen3-32B proportions of poles with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs.
Does not estimate those proportions across model sizes, dense/MoE architectures, or models up to trillions of parameters.
Does not study the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not test vision models or the proposed architectural, regularization, and tool explanations for interpretability.
Does not test attribution graphs or whether neurons suffice as circuit units.

Tests description prediction on generated text versus random control text, but not the specific claim that an explanation fits its activating examples and then fails on held-out natural activating examples.
Uses activation-based scoring on new text, but does not define a good-score threshold or report the fraction of individual neurons exceeding one.

relationships.condition: Single cluster descriptions (PRISM mean) of GPT-2 XL and Llama 3.1 8B neurons, and all description variants under non-default evaluation text generators
relationships.reason: Descriptions from top-activating clusters often fail to make the neuron fire on new text. Llama mean AUROC is 0.52 (r5, r6), GPT-2 XL mean is 0.61-0.65 (r1, r2, r19-r20, r23-r24, r27-r28, r31-r32, r35-r36), and scores fall near chance with other evaluation generators (r37-r44, r47-r48).
relationships.display_finding: Descriptions from top-activating clusters often failed to make the neuron fire on new text, with mean AUROC 0.52 for Llama and 0.61–0.65 for GPT-2 XL. With other evaluation text generators, scores fell near chance.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Single cluster descriptions (PRISM mean) of GPT-2 XL and Llama 3.1 8B neurons, and all description variants under non-default evaluation text generators
source_check.reason: Mean AUROC is 0.65 (GPT-2 XL) and 0.52 (Llama), and Qwen3 and Phi-4 evaluation give 0.53-0.61, so many descriptions fail to predict firing. Caveat: as worded, the condition also covers PRISM max with DeepSeek R1 evaluation (0.71, r45-r46), but those rows are listed under l1.

relationships.condition: Best-of-5 PRISM descriptions with the default Gemini evaluation generator
relationships.reason: Picking the best of five descriptions per neuron gives GPT-2 XL AUROC 0.85 with 91.67% positive MAD, and Llama 0.71 with 81.67% (r3, r4, r7, r8, r17-r18, r21-r22, r25-r26, r29-r30, r33-r34). Failure is then a minority, though the selection is on the test score, and with DeepSeek evaluation text it drops to 0.71 (r45-r46).
relationships.display_finding: AUROC reached 0.85 on GPT-2 XL with 91.67% positive MAD, and 0.71 on Llama with 81.67%, so failures became a minority. The best description is chosen on the test score, however, and with DeepSeek evaluation text the AUROC drops to 0.71.

relation.reason: The paper's own AUROC/MAD results on GPT-2 XL and Llama neurons bear on V6.

tranche.reason: Different method (cluster descriptions scored on LLM-generated concept text against Cosmopedia controls) aimed at whether descriptions built from activating examples predict neuron firing.

source_check.notes: All values match Tables 1, 4 and 5. They are means over 60 selected neurons from three layers (300 descriptions for the mean variant). Table 6 sanity check: randomly reassigned descriptions score max 0.65 / 66.67% and mean 0.52 / 49.33% on GPT-2 XL, so best-of-5 selection alone lifts random descriptions to 0.65. r45-r46 fall under l0's condition wording but are listed under l1.

statements.correction: GPT-2 XL PRISM max AUROC by evaluation generator (Table 5): Gemini 1.5 Pro 0.85 (0.78-0.91), Qwen3 32B 0.58 (0.46-0.69), Phi-4 0.61 (0.50-0.72), DeepSeek R1 0.71 (0.61-0.80); positive MAD 91.67%, 58.33%, 58.33%, 73.33%. PRISM mean AUROC: 0.65, 0.53, 0.54, 0.57. The authors call the drops 'slightly lower' and say the method ranking is preserved.
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but 'near chance with other evaluation generators' overgeneralizes. With DeepSeek R1 evaluation text, PRISM max keeps AUROC 0.71 (0.61-0.80).
